newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA GOALKEEPER DENIES HE BLUNDERED AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA GOALKEEPER DENIES HE BLUNDERED AGAIN.

text.p: Colombia goalkeeper Farid Mondragon denied on Sunday that he had committed yet another blunder in his team's last game against Mexico but he is expected to be dropped for the next match against Costa Rica.
Colombia coach Hernan Dario Gomez said there would be at least four changes to the team for Monday's Copa America group C match with Costa Rica and Mondragon is expected to be one of them.
Mondragon was blamed for the first goal as Colombia lost 2-1 to Mexico in their first game on Friday after he seemed to misjudge a speculative long-rage effort by Luis Hernandez.
"I don't see any reason why I have to feel guilty," he said. "It was an extremely powerful shot, there was a lot of wind and I didn't have time to react."

Mondragon's unhappy spell began with a bizarre mistake in a World Cup qualifier at home to Argentina when he thought a long-range shot was going out and let it pass, only to see it trickle into the net.
He was blamed for both the goals as Colombia lost 2-1 to Paraguay one month later and it was his poor clearance that allowed Peru to score the only goal of their next match.
